title: Laredo Illustrator Ricky Guerrero Brings a Bilingual Ghost to Life in 'Boooo Fantasma'
excerpt: Laredo-born illustrator Ricardo “Ricky” Guerrero, who went from doodling on Denny's napkins to illustrating for Little Golden Books, is the illustrator of “Boooo Fantasma: A Spooky Bilingual Halloween Book,” a bilingual board book blending Halloween and Día de los Muertos.
content:
Laredo-born illustrator Ricardo “Ricky” Guerrero, who once doodled on napkins while working as a waiter at Denny's, is now illustrating books for some of the biggest names in children's publishing — and his latest is a bilingual Halloween board book with a distinctly border flavor.

Guerrero illustrated “Boooo Fantasma: A Spooky Bilingual Halloween Book,” published by duopress labs, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The book follows a friendly ghost through Halloween and Día de los Muertos traditions, with text in English and Spanish and a Spanish glossary in the back, aimed at babies and toddlers.

His path to publishing is a Laredo story in itself. In an October 2026 profile in Tragaluz Journal titled “Ricardo Guerrero: from doodles to Disney,” Guerrero traced his start from doodling on napkins to becoming a published illustrator for Little Golden Books, including illustrating “The X-Files: Is the Truth Out There?” He credits 1990s Goosebumps books, artist Mary Blair and illustrator Tim Jacobus among his influences, and says the film Frozen 2 pushed him to pursue art seriously.

Guerrero was accepted into the Scholastic Mentorship Program and has worked as a colorist on Scholastic's “Skibidi Toilet” original graphic novel “Cosmic Threats,” due out March 2, according to the Laredo Morning Times. He also showed his work at Light Box Expo 2025.

Closer to home, Guerrero painted a mural at Molina Grizzlies school, and the Laredo Public Library's McKendrick Ochoa Salinas branch hosted him as a special guest for its Teen Spooky Watercolor Art event on Oct. 21, featuring him alongside his book.

For a city that rarely sees its own artists on national bookstore shelves, Guerrero's rise — from napkin doodles to Little Golden Books and Scholastic — is a reminder that Laredo talent travels.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 26, 2026; Tragaluz Journal, October 2026, “Ricardo Guerrero: from doodles to Disney” by Mario E. Martinez; Laredo Public Library, Oct. 14, 2026.
